title: Usage signal forensics & roadmap commitment - QBR
meeting_header: Date: 2027-03-21 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Jonah Ruiz (Redwood SE), Elena Kline (Redwood CSM); Priya Shah (NovumGrid VP Product), Liam O'Neil (Platform Eng), Sofia Martinez (DevOps), Rajiv Banerjee (FinOps)
summary: Quarterly check-in focused on dissecting signal of usage spikes, cost drivers, and reliability gaps. Reviewed recent burst event, latency tail, and upcoming roadmap commitments (pilot expansion, model rollouts). Agreed on a 2-week pilot benchmarking window, security docs share, and a cost-optimization playbook to evaluate batching and KV cache settings.
topics: latency tail vs unit cost tradeoffs
dedicated vs hosted choice for pilot
security/compliance ask: SOC2 + KMS + audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Priya Shah: Priya here. Liam, Sofia, Rajiv with me.
[00:15] Jonah Ruiz: Jonah from Redwood, SE. I'll jump into the usage graphs in a bit.
[00:22] Maya Patel: Cool. Agenda, quick forensic on last week's spike, cost drivers, reliability notes, then roadmap ask and next steps.
[00:32] Liam O'Neil: We saw a sharp increase in token usage on Thursday night, about 3x baseline for 20 minutes. It coincided with a campaign but some calls had high 95th-percentile latency where our service started to time out.
[00:46] Jonah Ruiz: Right, I pulled the trace — looks like a workload pattern with short bursts and lots of small prompts, so it's actually not per-request token heavy but concurrency spiky which hits queuing. Our autoscaler did spin up, but the queueing added tail latency.
[01:05] Sofia Martinez: We were on hosted, default batching. We hadn't set prefix caching at the time.
[01:12] Maya Patel: That's a great signal. Two things: batching and KV/prefix cache can shrink token work and reduce hot-path cost. Also consider pinning a model variant with a lower context memory footprint when you expect short prompts.
[01:28] Priya Shah: The finance team noticed the bill jump. Rajiv, can you explain the unit-cost view?
[01:35] Rajiv Banerjee: Sure. We saw per-hour spend double on GPU-backed calls during the spike. Some of that is under the hood — e.g., the runtime kept warm replicas for fast cold-starts. It felt like we paid for throughput we didn't fully utilize.
[01:50] Jonah Ruiz: We can run a quick cost profile: trade off warm replicas vs latency SLO. We also recommend setting a burst policy that allows occasional overage with throttled routing to a cheaper variant for non-critical routes.
[02:05] Liam O'Neil: Curious on dedicated vs hosted. If we move to Dedicated, do we get better predictability on those bursts?
[02:13] Jonah Ruiz: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolated pools, which helps tail latency, yes. But it comes with commitment costs. For an initial phase, we suggest a short reserved cap + autoscale burst to hosted as fallback — that hybrid often hits both cost and latency goals.
[02:28] Priya Shah: Can you quantify the break-even?
[02:31] Maya Patel: We'll send a break-even model. Quick answer — if your sustained baseline is above X tokens/hour (we'll compute), Dedicated tends to be more economical, otherwise hybrid or hosted tuned with caching wins.
[02:45] Sofia Martinez: On security: the procurement team requested SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML integration, audit logs retention, and KMS support for key management.
[02:56] Elena Kline: We have SOC2 Type II artifacts and a VPC/private deployment checklist. KMS/HSM is supported in Private mode; for hosted we offer customer-managed keys via supported KMS integrations. We'll share the security pack.
[03:15] Priya Shah: Also need data residency for EU workload segments.
[03:19] Maya Patel: We can route EU traffic to EU regions and provide audit logs per-region.
[03:25] Rajiv Banerjee: For the cost playbook, we need specifics on batching parameters and suggested quantization settings — we tried an aggressive int8 config last month and saw some quality regressions.
[03:38] Jonah Ruiz: Noted. We'll give a tiered recommendation: conservative quantization for latency-sensitive flows, experimental quant profiles for non-critical flows. We'll also attach prompt sets for you to validate.
[03:52] Liam O'Neil: For the forensic — any suspicious errors in the logs? Did we see retries stacking?
[03:59] Jonah Ruiz: There were a few client-side retries at ten-second intervals; some causing duplicate load. We recommend jittered backoff and idempotency keys on your side. Also increase short-term concurrency limits in the SDK to smooth the burst.
[04:20] Priya Shah: On roadmap, we want to expand pilot to 3 additional product routes by May. Can you commit to a benchmark window?
[04:29] Maya Patel: Yes — proposed 2-week pilot starting April 4th to measure latency, p95/p99, and cost delta across three variants: hosted tuned, hosted with prefix cache, and small Dedicated pool.
[04:42] Rajiv Banerjee: That works for finance — we'll sign off conditional on the pilot's cost projection.
[04:47] Sofia Martinez: In terms of telemetry, can we get token-level breakdowns per route and per-token latency histograms?
[04:55] Jonah Ruiz: Absolutely. We'll supply a metrics dashboard with per-route token split, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and canonical traces you can jump into.
[05:06] Maya Patel: I'll also include a recorded walkthrough of the dashboard.
[05:10] Priya Shah: One ask — competitor benchmarking. We ran a quick test with ApexAI and they had lower nominal latency but their callbacks failed more. Can Redwood run a side-by-side on our sample workloads?
[05:22] Jonah Ruiz: We can run a comparo as long as you provide the sample prompt set and allowed endpoints. We'll need written consent for third-party testing — just to stay compliant.
[05:34] Liam O'Neil: Fine. We'll give you a redacted prompt set.
[05:38] Maya Patel: Cool. Any other risks we should call out?
[05:42] Priya Shah: Model rollout safety. We had one false-positive classification when we switched to a newer variant last month.
[05:49] Elena Kline: We recommend canary rollouts + automatic fallback to previous model on quality regressions; Redwood's rollout policies can do canary percentages and automatic metrics-based rollback.
[06:03] Rajiv Banerjee: Will fallback preserve session context? We had KV cache warmup concerns.
[06:09] Jonah Ruiz: When fallback occurs, session continuity can be preserved with shared KV caches in the same pool, but cross-variant cache reuse depends on model tokenizer alignment. We'll outline limits in the playbook.
[06:22] Sofia Martinez: Operationally, we'd like an on-call playbook for spike handling — who do we ping at Redwood?
[06:29] Maya Patel: Primary SE contact is Jonah; for incidents Elena is CSM lead. We'll provide escalation contacts and an incident runbook tailored to your routes.
[06:40] Priya Shah: Sounds good. If the pilot meets bar, what's the typical procurement timeline for Dedicated?
[06:46] Maya Patel: Procurement + security review + contract usually takes 4–8 weeks depending on legal cycles. We'll try to compress by prepping SOC2 and procurement templates ahead of time.
[06:58] Liam O'Neil: Are there any hidden fees around data egress or extra observability retention?
[07:03] Maya Patel: Observability retention beyond the default window is an add-on. Data egress depends on region-to-region transfers; we'll include estimates.
[07:12] Priya Shah: Ok let's recap next steps.
[07:15] Maya Patel: Recap: 1) Redwood to share security pack and SOC2 artifacts; 2) Jonah to provide cost break-even model and recommended batching/quantization playbook; 3) Schedule pilot for April 4th (2 weeks) across three variants; 4) Redwood to deliver per-route dashboard and side-by-side benchmark plan.
[07:36] Priya Shah: I'll coordinate schedule internally and confirm pilot routes.
[07:40] Rajiv Banerjee: Finance will review break-even and sign pilot PO if numbers make sense.
[07:45] Maya Patel: Great. Any other open Qs?
[07:48] Sofia Martinez: None here.
[07:50] Jonah Ruiz: I'll attach example SDK settings for jittered backoff and idempotency keys.
[07:55] Maya Patel: Thank you all. We'll follow up with notes and links.
[08:00] Priya Shah: Thanks, bye.
[08:02] [meeting ended]

Note: transcript has occasional mis-heard words (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cache", "quantization" appears as "quantize shun" in a few spots). Some speaker attributions may be approximate.

Redwood to provide security docs and technical playbooks to reduce spike-driven costs using batching, prefix/KV caching, and rollout safeguards.
